hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxides change across the period, from ionic and basic on the left to covalent and acidic on the right.
Remember that $\text{MgO}$ is basic and giant ionic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and giant ionic, while $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic and giant covalent.
Think about which of these three oxides can actually dissolve or react with water, and which are completely insoluble solids.
walkthrough:
**Recall the acid-base trend**

Think of the oxides from left to right. Basic character decreases and acidic character increases.

$\text{MgO}$ is basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric (reacts with both acids and bases), $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic.

**Recall the structure and melting point trend**

$\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ are both giant ionic lattices, so they have very high melting points.

$\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent lattice (like diamond), so it also has a very high melting point, not a low one.

**Check reaction with water**

$\text{MgO}$ reacts slightly with water to give a sparingly soluble hydroxide:
$$\text{MgO(s) + H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$$
This gives a weakly alkaline solution of about pH 9.

**Conclude the correct row**

Both $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and show no reaction with water.

So the only row with slight reaction, no reaction, no reaction is correct.

options.A: The first two entries are right, $\text{MgO}$ is basic and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric. However $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic, not amphoteric. It reacts with hot concentrated alkali but not with acids, so this row fails on the last column.
options.B: $\text{MgO}$ is indeed giant ionic, but $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is also giant ionic, not simple molecular. $\text{SiO}_2$ is giant covalent (macromolecular), not giant ionic and not simple molecular. Two errors make this row wrong.
options.C: $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ do have high melting points due to strong ionic bonding. The trap is $\text{SiO}_2$, which also has a very high melting point (about 1610 C) because of its strong giant covalent network. It does not have a low melting point.
options.D: This is fully correct. $\text{MgO}$ reacts slightly with water to form $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, giving a pH around 9. Both $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble solids that show no reaction with water.
